steps.description: Registered session 1 (github-copilot / claude-opus-5, high).

Caption renamed to AI Work Explorer, decided by PROBING a running workbench rather than by reading the manifest. Baseline probe: container title 'AI Orch' + view name 'Work Explorer' renders `.part.sidebar .title-label` as 'AI Orch: Work Explorer', and the single view's pane header is display:none (merged into the container title). Candidate probe: setting container title, view name AND contextualTitle all to 'AI Work Explorer' renders exactly 'AI Work Explorer' -- a single-view container joins the two names with a colon UNLESS they are identical, which is why Set 123 S3 restoring the container title ALONE would have given back AI WORK EXPLORER: WORK EXPLORER. Sibling site fixed in the same pass (L-069-1): the aria-label substring selector in src/test/playwright/electronLaunch.ts openDabblerContainer, which is how every Layer 3 spec opens the sidebar at all. New Layer 3 spec sidebar-caption.spec.ts asserts the RENDERED header rather than the manifest fields, with two falsifiers: no colon (the join survived) and exactly one occurrence of 'Work Explorer' (the Set 123 defect). Both were PLANTED and confirmed to fire (L-112-1): reverting the view name produced the observed string 'AI Work Explorer: Work Explorer'; reverting the container title to AI Orch timed out openDabblerContainer on the aria-label, which proves the harness-selector coupling the spec warned would fail silently. No stale current-state echo remains -- every surviving 'AI Orch' hit is a historical Set 123 record.

closeOutSummary returns an empty string for state=absent instead of 'not computed' (operator ruling, 2026-08-14). The readiness answer renders in the same gray slot as the projection's own 'as of HH:MM' timestamp -- stepDescriptor joins [started, readiness] since Set 129 -- so an EMPTY slot already says no answer has been computed, and the phrase was a second rendering of a fact the row already carried. Set 127 S2's rule survives, enforced rather than worded: the rewritten unit test 'absent is still distinguishable from a clean row' asserts the absent row has no phrase AND no 'as of', while a settled all-met projection IS dated and takes done.svg -- different description, different icon. The test was rewritten, not deleted, as the spec required. Layer 3 got a free assertion inside work-explorer-steps (that fixture never writes a projection, so its close step IS the absent case): no rendered row contains 'not computed'. The extension README's four-states line was updated to match. 78/78 workExplorerTreeModel unit tests green; tsc --noEmit clean; the 9 eslint errors are pre-existing, all in files this session did not touch.

Cross-provider verification, 3 rounds, verifier gpt-5.5 (anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's registry-resolved effective provider). Round 1 discovery, fan-out 2 (spec-conformance + failure-scenario lenses): ISSUES_FOUND, 1 Major -- workExplorerMenuParity.test.ts still asserted the retired view name 'Work Explorer', which would have left the whole extension suite red. Decisive and correct: my sibling sweep searched for the container title 'AI Orch' and never for the view NAME, and the file that holds it calls itself 'the ONE place the shipping identity is asserted', which is exactly why nothing else caught it. Round 2 supplementary (run BEFORE any remediation, per loop discipline): VERIFIED, nothing new; session verdict stayed ISSUES_FOUND because the discovery blocker stood. Remediated beyond the literal -- the old assertion pinned one of three fields that must agree, so updating it alone would have re-armed the trap; a second test now asserts container title == view name == contextualTitle, which closes the CLASS (L-069-1). Proven by planting: drifting contextualTitle to 'AI Orch' failed the new test at line 118, then restored green. Also ran the FULL Layer 2 mocha suite as part of remediation rather than the single module file, since narrow scoping is what let the finding through: 1456 passing / 0 failing / 2 pending. acceptance_harness round 1 recorded the judgment criterion as never auto-closable. Round 3 remediation-review over the fix delta: VERIFIED, 1 fix accepted, 0 rejected, 0 findings. Sidecar: s1-remediation-round-1.md. Bounds untouched -- 1 discovery pass and 1 remediation-review cycle used of 2 each.

Required portion = all three declared suites, named by `run_of_record affected` over this session's 27 changed paths, run AFTER the last code change (A2/L-064-12) and each recorded. pytest: 4490 passed, 9 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed, 1178s. mocha: 1456 passing, 2 pending (pre-existing), 0 failing, 84s. playwright: 32/32 executed and passed, recorded as a DISCLOSED COMPOSITE -- one full invocation went 29 passed / 3 failed in 9.4m at 4 workers, and all three failures passed when re-run in isolation immediately afterward (native-tree + session-plan-reveal together, 58.2s; vsix-first-run-walkthrough alone, 71s against the 300s timeout it exhausted under load). That last one is the chronic flake this set's own spec already names as residual R2, and the config file documents the same small-runner contention mode. Under project-guidance -> Practicality outranks rule-perfectionism, the test is 'did every test execute and pass', not 'did it happen in one invocation' -- same specs, same assertions, nothing skipped, weakened or accepted red. The composition is journaled in decisions.jsonl and stated in the disposition rather than presented as a clean single run. run_of_record check: all three [ok] fresh and green. Also clean: tsc --noEmit; the 9 eslint errors are pre-existing in six files this session never opened.
Close-out.
Registered session 2 (github-copilot / claude-opus-5, high).

Fix D1: replaced the 0-3-space indent cap in _STEP_RE with _top_level_step_starts, a CommonMark nesting scan (a marker at or past the innermost open item's content column is a sub-step). Set 131 S1 now parses at its declared 6, not 11. Corpus-wide: 374 sessions, 2030 -> 2005 steps, 5 sessions changed (002 S4 6->0, 022 S1 9->6, 022 S2 10->6, 107 S1 16->9, 131 S1 11->6), all verified correct by hand. Also decided and shipped the exit-code half: --spec now exits non-zero on a failed admission, --all stays a census unless --check (journaled).

Fix D2: added classify_steps()/work_step_count() and SessionPlan.work_step_count. Ceremony is a role the skeleton assigns by POSITION (first slot, last three) CONFIRMED BY naming; everything else is work however much of a stage it quotes. intents_named stays the mention primitive check_step_shape needs. Corrected N: Set 132 = 2/3/3, Set 131 = 2/2/2, exactly as the spec asserts. 28 falsifiers in ai_router/tests/test_spec_admission_step_counting.py; 9 planted defects, all 9 caught (L-112-1).

Re-ran the Set 131 probe on the fixed instrument over 225 qualifying sessions (both instruments on identical rows). Published docs/session-sets/132-.../s2-measurement.md. Direction held but weakly: corr(N,total) +0.202 -> +0.224; corr(N,min/step) -0.191 -> -0.107. N changed in 90 of 225 (mean 2.83 -> 3.26). PRIMARY RESULT (the tail): duration is elapsed CALENDAR time, 15 sessions crossed a night and ALL 15 are in the 23 longest; p90 falls 301 -> 147 excluding them, 311 -> 140 idle-trimmed, robust across idle caps 20-120m with zero ceiling hits. Call it D3. Also: refitting total = F + N*wbar on corrected N gives POSITIVE F everywhere (OLS 20-41, Theil-Sen 35-39), so the spec's 'constant wbar does not fit the data' argument (which rested on an impossible F = -16) does not survive; F=39/wbar=8.4 predicts observed per-step medians within ~1 min for N=2..4. Cap unchanged. Corrected the now-false 'longest sessions on record (591,562,544,509)' claim in both echoes (module docstring + authoring guide) and shipped an ai_router changelog fragment.

Round 1 discovery, fan-out 2/2 (gpt-5.5, both lenses; anthropic excluded as the orchestrator provider): VERIFIED, 0 blocking, 3 Minor nits. All three were accuracy defects in my own prose and all three were fixed before the suite ran: (1) the measurement's Short Version credited the fixed instrument for overturning the spec's 'constant wbar does not fit' argument, when Section 4 shows the old instrument's N also fits positive F -- the artifact was the two-point band-median fit, not the deflated N; (2) the over-cap count was inconsistent (48 vs 50) and BOTH were wrong -- a precise recount gives 51->48 raw, 50->47 without a declared exception, across 32->31 specs, and every shipping surface now says 47/31; (3) 's2-measurement.md' told a re-runner to use 'git show HEAD:' for the pre-fix module, which is only true while uncommitted -- it now names the parent revision. s2-conventions.md was corrected in place with the correction called out inline; the raw verification artifacts were not touched.

run_of_record affected named all three suites (pytest, mocha and playwright each declare ai_router/ in covers), so all three were fully run after the last code change and recorded. pytest 4519 passed / 9 skipped (12m18s) -- up 29 from S1's 4490, which is the new falsifier module. mocha 1456 passing / 0 failing / 2 pending (50s). playwright recorded as a DISCLOSED COMPOSITE: the full run went 30 passed / 2 failed and both failures passed in isolation immediately after (session-plan-reveal 2/2 in 33s; vsix-first-run-walkthrough 1/1 in 1.2m against the 300s timeout it had exhausted under load) -- the same load-sensitive flakes S1 disclosed, on extension code this session does not touch. All 32 executed and passed; composition journaled. No test skipped, weakened or accepted red.

close_session succeeded at 15:41. All blocking gates PASS (working_tree_clean, pushed_to_remote, verification_integrity, test_run_fresh, uat_walk_recorded, activity_log_entry, next_orchestrator_present, change_log_fresh, verification_method_vocabulary); one advisory WARN on checklist_posted for the close-out transition, cleared by the post recorded immediately after. session-state.json flipped to complete/closed by the sanctioned writer; progress projection regenerated. Cost at close (floor): 2560.7 credits / \.61 -- orchestrator seat 2244.8 (lower bound, this conversation still in flight), routed Copilot CLI 315.9 measured, Direct API not applicable.
Registered session 3 (github-copilot / claude-opus-5, high).

Panel run in two rounds (generate-diverse then adversarial cross-critique) across two GENUINE providers -- openai gpt-5.5 and google gemini-3.1-pro-preview -- after discovering that route(prefer_model=) is silently dropped by the copilot-cli transport (it resolves one generator ROLE, not a tier ladder), which had sent all four first-attempt generations to gpt-5.5. Repaired via exclude_providers=[anthropic, openai], the lever that path DOES honour; the two mislabeled artifacts were renamed -openai-sample-2, not edited. Both providers independently: the candidate design is sound-with-modifications but must not use self-reported effort (primary outcome becomes a blinded Extra Work Score over atomized obligations), the uncapped arm is CONFOUNDED not merely less relevant (cap-4 if a third point is wanted), one spec is not evidence, and nobody knows the paired SD until a pilot runs. Both then said the same unprompted thing: given the observational numbers, do not fund the generative experiment at all yet. The observational fallback was RUN rather than merely evaluated (97 sessions): F = 41 min measured directly from ceremony-step timestamps against a regression intercept of 39 from an independent method, w-bar = 6.4 min, corr(N, w-bar) = -0.03 to -0.17. Fixed overhead is 5-7x a work step, which makes N second-order. The composition artifact both were asked to attack was confirmed (skeleton-era share falls 59% -> 0% as N rises) and the skeleton-era cut is honestly reported as able to validate F but NOT the N slope, because the cap itself removed the variance.

Answered inside the existing rubric, and the answer is that NOTHING is added: no gate, no config key, no CLI, no close-out predicate. L-095-1's consequence test (probability x impact), already promoted into project-guidance.md and already preload, IS the operator's question -- evaluated about a proposed step instead of a reported finding. Shipped as a scope statement in the authoring guide's *Other sizing signals*, beside the sizing rules it modifies: name the failure scenario that follows from NOT doing a step; no nameable scenario means it is a nit and does not belong in the plan. It is a removal tool by construction -- no branch of it can add a step -- which makes it an instance of *Prefer removal over addition*, not an exception. project-guidance.md was deliberately NOT edited: the spec made that touch conditional ('only if the rubric genuinely extends') and the rule does not change, only its application point, which belongs where plan authoring is documented. That call also kept the file under its preload ceiling -- a first draft that did edit it breached by 126 tokens, and ceilings ratchet down only. Priced honestly against this session's own measurement: ~7 min per step removed, real and an order below the ceremony beside it.

Compaction trigger fixed at ~150K retained input tokens, first step boundary after the crossing -- Set 131 S3's numbers, unmoved. What this session ADDS is the half that stops it being every boundary, and the coupling. The arithmetic is self-defeating rather than merely unprofitable: a flush RESETS the transcript to ~54K, inside the cheap 25-75K plateau, so a second flush at the next boundary pays the full 400 credits to save approximately nothing. A session at N=3 has 7 steps and 6 internal boundaries; firing at all six costs 2,400 credits of which at most the first can repay. Stated as a contract: the boundary says WHEN it is safe to flush, the threshold says WHETHER it is worth flushing, and both are required. The coupling now lives in one place (workflow doc, new subsection): N determines how many boundaries EXIST, the threshold determines which of them FIRE, with the obligation named in both directions -- a set that lowers N must check the remaining boundaries still land near 150K, one that lowers the threshold must check it has not recreated the every-boundary policy. Tied to this session's own measurement: corr(N, F) = +0.267 is the shape you would expect if a longer context-heavy session pays more at its close, and rotation attacks that without touching N. Education-mode brief on N delivered in s3-causality-and-compaction.md section 7: recommendation KEEP N=3, high confidence the evidence does not support raising it and that N is the wrong lever at all (F is 5-7x a work step), low confidence 3 is optimal because the cap itself removed the variance needed to find an optimum; default on no answer is that N stays 3.

Round 1 discovery, fan-out 2/2 (gpt-5.5, spec-conformance + failure-scenario lenses; anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's registry-resolved provider): VERIFIED, 0 findings. Then the set-terminal PATH-AWARE CRITIQUE, which is armed advisory and is code-changing, so it ran BEFORE the suites per the Step 8 ordering. The automated producer refused -- pull_verifier has no transport awareness and hard-requires DABBLER_* keys -- so the manual flow the template calls the default was used, driven through routed children, which on this transport carry --available-tools view,grep,glob and are therefore genuinely path-aware. Two distinct providers forced by exclusion (gpt-5.5; gemini-3.1-pro-preview). BOTH returned ISSUES_FOUND and both independently found the same two Majors, which is what makes them credible: (1) the claim that per-role totals are robust to batch logging holds only WITHIN a role -- a batch crossing work/ceremony misattributes; (2) the two F estimates are NOT independent, and gemini's version was decisive arithmetic: my work+ceremony totals sum by construction to completedAt-startedAt, exactly the interval S2 regressed. gpt-5.5 added two more: the 129-session step_number_outside_parse exclusion was undisclosed, and the causal wording in the short version, the operator brief, the authoring guide and the change-log outran the document's own section 8. All four remediated by MEASURING rather than rewording where possible: the probe now counts mixed-role batches (10 of 97) and reports the cut without them -- w-bar unchanged at 6.4, corr -0.029 -> -0.027, F rising 41.1 -> 47.0, so the conclusion survives -- and counts exclusions by reason, which also showed the drop is NOT era-concentrated (050s-130s). Independence claim corrected everywhere including the changelog fragment; causal wording downgraded to 'strongest observed discriminator' in all four echoes. path-aware-critique.json assembled from the raw verdicts and validates (code=valid, 2 distinct providers). post_round_delta then classified the remediation as A4.2 shipped-code, so ONE delta-scoped remediation-review was run: VERIFIED, 3 fix-accepted + 1 accepted-with-modification, 0 rejected, 2 Minor nits (stale docstring echo; 'same-second' vs exact-timestamp grouping) both fixed in place. Bounds: 1 discovery and 1 remediation-review used of 2 each.

Required portion = all three suites. run_of_record affected named them because this session's changelog fragment lands under ai_router/, which mocha and playwright both declare in covers, and pytest additionally covers docs/session-sets/. Each run AFTER the last code change and recorded. pytest 4519 passed / 9 skipped (pre-existing) / 0 failed. mocha 1456 passing / 0 failing / 2 pending (pre-existing), 37s. playwright recorded as a DISCLOSED COMPOSITE: the full invocation went 31 passed / 1 failed in 8.2m, the failure being vsix-first-run-walkthrough exhausting its 300s budget waiting on a tree row under load; re-run alone immediately afterward it passed in 43.3s. All 32 scenarios executed and passed; nothing skipped, weakened or accepted red. That spec is this set's own named residual R2 and this is the third consecutive session to record the same composition on it, which is the argument for retiring or de-flaking it rather than for re-litigating it here. Journaled as goal-over-letter. pytest was then RE-RUN and re-recorded: the operator's N ruling arrived after the first recording and edited s3-causality-and-compaction.md, which lives under docs/session-sets/ and therefore binds pytest's surface digest (change-log.md and the lifecycle ledgers are exempt as bookkeeping; session WORK is not). Paying an 12-minute re-run is the honest cost of a late decision -- the alternative was to let a recorded run predate the content it covers. All three now report fresh and green.
Close-out, including the Step 9 reorganization review.
